[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
A '''Robert Glasgow''' was recorded at Inveresk and Musselburgh, Midlothian, on 30 December 1627, with his father indexed as Allexander Glasgow.<ref name="Birth1627">Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms, Inveresk and Musselburgh parish 689, reference 10/171, Robert Glasgow, 30 December 1627. See also [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-58S FamilySearch record VQ4V-58S].</ref> The identification of that child with the later Edinburgh-area husband and cordiner is chronologically plausible but has not been proved by a record naming his age or parentage.

=== The Euphame household ===

Scotland's People indexes the following children to a Robert Glasgow and Euphame Lorimer or Laurimer:

* Eupham, 8 May 1651 at Edinburgh, reference 685/1 50/395;
* Kathrin, 3 February 1659 at St Cuthbert's, reference 685/2 30/28;
* William, 29 November 1662 at St Cuthbert's, reference 685/2 30/53; and
* Magdalene, 14 August 1664 at Edinburgh, reference 685/1 60/377.<ref name="LorimerChildren">Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms: Eupham Glasgow, 8 May 1651, Edinburgh 685/1 50/395; Kathrin Glasgow, 3 February 1659, St Cuthbert's 685/2 30/28; William Glasgow, 29 November 1662, St Cuthbert's 685/2 30/53; Magdalene Glasgow, 14 August 1664, Edinburgh 685/1 60/377. Parents indexed as Robert Glasgow and Euphame Lorimer/Laurimer. See also [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F316-JRS FamilySearch record for William].</ref>

On 4 July 1666 a Robert Glasgow, cordiner, was admitted burgess of Edinburgh by right of his wife Euphame, daughter of the late Andrew Lorimer, beltmaker and burgess.<ref name="Burgess1666">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=218 ''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1929), printed p. 208.</ref> The name, wife and dates make him very probably the father in this Lorimer household.

A separate entry for Jonet Glasgow on 1 January 1657 names parents Robert Glasgow and Eupham Tailyour, St Cuthbert's reference 685/2 30/15.<ref name="Jonet1657">Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms, St Cuthbert's 685/2 30/15, Jonet Glasgow, 1 January 1657, parents indexed as Robert Glasgow and Eupham Tailyour; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTRF-N6K FamilySearch derivative index].</ref> Tailyour and Lorimer must not be treated as the same woman without inspection of the original entries or other connecting evidence.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1148]] is assessed at 97% (proved). Robert’s 30 December 1627 Inveresk baptism names Allexander Glasgow. The selected Alexander account represents the local father whose children run from 1626 to 1637, with the same family later explicitly naming Janet Clerk. This supports the recorded child’s father strongly.

The 1627 child’s parentage, not proof that he became the later Edinburgh cordiner or husband.

Next useful test: Test the child-to-cordiner identity with an age, apprenticeship or kinship record.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-58S Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms, Inveresk and Musselburgh parish 689, reference 10/171, Robert Glasgow, 30 December 1627. See also FamilySearch record VQ4V-58S (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-58S).]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.



The records strongly reconstruct an adult Robert-and-Euphame Lorimer household in and around Edinburgh from 1651 to 1666. They do not yet prove that its Robert was the child recorded at Inveresk in 1627. The original parish images, cordiner records, marriage evidence and testamentary material remain the best targets.

The Lorimer household also brackets the 1 July 1652 marriage of a different cordiner Robert Glasgow to Jonet Thomsone. It therefore strongly weakens the earlier suggestion that the 1652 bridegroom later became the 1666 burgess.

=== North Leith namesake, 1694 ===

The original North Leith poll-tax page lists a '''Robert Glasgow''' among four servants in the household of Alexander Ainslie, clerk to the glass manufactory, on 3 October 1694.<ref name="Leith1694">National Records of Scotland, Scottish Exchequer poll tax, North Leith parish, E70/4/10, image 11, 3 October 1694; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/virtual-volumes/volume-images/volume_data-E70-4-10/REX01666?image_number=11 original image], Scotland's People Virtual Volumes.</ref> A later thesis describes Robert as a glassmaker, but the original calls him only a servant. On 16 July 1694 a Robert Glasgow gave a receipt in Ainslie's name for bottles supplied to the Earl of Breadalbane.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Breadalbane Muniments, GD112/15/59, item 24, 16 July 1694, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD112%2F15%2F59 catalogue description].</ref> The shared employer and year make him almost certainly the October servant and prove a functional glassworks-business role, though not that he was a skilled glassmaker. This profile's Robert would have been 66. The Midlothian setting and chronology make comparison worthwhile, but no record connects the Ainslie servant with Euphame Lorimer or this household.


[[Glasgow-3011|Robert Glasgow]], baptised at Glencorse in 1676, is a stronger younger chronological candidate: he was seventeen in 1694, is the only exact-name Robert baptism returned for Glencorse from 1640 through 1690, and a same-name man married there in 1704. There is still no direct Ainslie or glassworks link.

Exact Scotland's People OPR searches found no Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascow, Glaskow or Glassgow baptism in the Leith parishes from 1694 to 1730, and no exact Robert Glasgow marriage there from 1694 to 1710 or burial from 1694 to 1730. Register survival and spelling limit those negative results.
